problem: Build a small social graph where some profiles belong to pets rather than people. Write a walker that starts at each person and recommends new friends, but only adult human ones -- pet profiles and minors must never show up in the suggestions. Print how many raw neighbours each person sees versus how many survive the filters.

Model a city as stations connected to hotels and attractions, each attraction carrying a star rating. From every station, shortlist only the attractions (ignore hotels) and then only those rated 4 stars or higher, and print the final itinerary.

Our power-grid model stores transmission lines between substations, each carrying its capacity in megawatts. Walk the grid from every substation and list only the neighbours reachable over lines rated above 400 MW -- weaker lines can't carry the scheduled transfer.

Each delivery route from our depots carries a cargo weight in tonnes. A truck may only be dispatched when its load is at least 2 tonnes and at most 8 tonnes on the same leg. Check every depot and print which routes qualify for dispatch.
Given a co-authorship graph of researchers, suggest collaboration contacts for each researcher: people exactly two co-authored links away who are neither themselves nor direct co-authors already.

Our knowledge wiki has articles citing other articles, and articles written by authors. Starting from one article, follow its citations onward to discover the authors behind the cited work, mixing both relationship kinds in a single walk.

Store a family tree as parent-to-child links. For every person, work out their siblings by going up to their shared parents and back down to the other children, and report each person's full sibling list.

We run several depots that each serve a set of stores. Instead of checking depots one by one, anchor one combined query from the whole list of depot nodes at once, find every store within reach, and flag the ones whose stock has dropped below 20 units.

Print a fare board for our flight network. The flights themselves carry the data -- flight number and ticket price -- so read the connections themselves rather than just the destination airports, and list every departure from each airport with its fare.

Metro stations are linked by typed route edges carrying a line colour and travel time in minutes. For every station, find the fastest line departing from it, and print a connection board of station-to-station routes with their lines and durations.

Send a delivery van from our depot across town to Seaside. Every road charges a toll collected as the van crosses it, and the van should keep a running total of tolls paid, printing the bill at each town it arrives in and the grand total at the end.

Our power grid's lines meter current as inspectors cross them. Audit the grid twice: once walking substation to substation normally, and once in a mode where the inspector steps onto each line itself. Show that meters only record in the second mode.

A courier serves districts either by highway or by ferry depending on the dispatch mode chosen at run time. Run two deliveries with different modes and let the courier pick which kind of connection to follow while it walks, reporting where each run can and cannot go.

Program a warehouse robot whose route plan says, per cell, whether it should roll along the floor or climb stairs to the mezzanine. The robot reads its plan as it goes, follows only the allowed movement kind out of each cell, and logs the path it took.

Audit a project folder tree and flag files larger than 100 KB. Traverse depth-first -- fully explore each subdirectory before moving to the next one -- and print the entry trail so the dive order is visible.

Simulate contact tracing from patient zero through a network of contacts. The outbreak should spread wave by wave: everyone exposed in a wave gets contacted before the next wave starts. Print the contact sequence so the level-by-level order is evident.

Trace water through a pipeline from the intake valve. Some valves are capped stubs with no outgoing pipe; the tracer should note each dead end gracefully instead of stalling, and summarize the full route and how many dead ends it hit.

In a parcel sorting hub, look up the destination bin for an incoming parcel first, then route the parcel through conveyor junctions straight toward that stored bin object -- no repeated searching at junctions -- and stop the moment it is delivered.

Our build system's dependency graph contains diamonds: shared libraries are needed by several modules. Count total build minutes across all tasks, making sure a task reachable by multiple paths is audited exactly once even though traversal reaches it more than once.

Audit our warehouse inventory graph: give every item's stable unique id so external systems can reference it, persist each item to storage during the walk, and finish by dumping the graph structure hanging off the root for a visual sanity check.
